questions.question: The width of a doorway should ideally be at least:
questions.explanation: A 36-inch (about 90 cm) door allows wheelchair access.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A toilet seat height of ______ is considered optimal for a wheelchair user.
questions.explanation: A raised seat of 17-19 inches matches the wheelchair seat for transfers.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The C in PICO, which is used to formulate a clinical question, stands for:
questions.explanation: PICO is Patient/Problem, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of levels of evidence from highest to lowest?

options.A: Systematic review, RCT, cohort studies, case-control studies, case report, expert opinion
options.B: RCT, systematic review, cohort, case-control, expert opinion, case report
options.C: Expert opinion, case report, case-control, cohort, RCT, systematic review
options.D: Cohort studies, RCT, systematic review, case report, expert opinion

questions.explanation: Evidence is ranked from systematic reviews and RCTs down to expert opinion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following data sources is NOT considered primary?
questions.explanation: Newspaper accounts are secondary sources.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which type of research studies complex human behaviour?
questions.explanation: Qualitative research explores meaning, experience and behaviour.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following research designs is NOT quantitative in nature?
questions.explanation: Case studies are generally qualitative.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following research designs is NOT qualitative in nature?
questions.explanation: Quasi-experimental designs are quantitative.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The association between exposure and outcome is studied in:
questions.explanation: Analytic studies (cohort, case-control) test hypotheses about exposure and outcome.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which studies are employed to describe the occurrence of an outcome?
questions.explanation: Descriptive studies document who, where and when.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a randomised controlled trial (RCT)?

options.A: All of these: it is costly, complex and time-consuming

questions.explanation: RCTs need large resources and long follow-up.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the correlation coefficient is near +1, then:

options.B: There is a strong positive correlation between the variables

questions.explanation: r near +1 indicates variables rise together.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the correlation coefficient is near 0, then:

options.A: There is a strong negative correlation
options.C: There is no correlation between the variables
options.D: There is a strong positive correlation

questions.explanation: r near 0 indicates no linear relationship.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an experimental research study, the independent variable is the:
questions.explanation: The independent variable is manipulated by the researcher.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an experimental research study, the dependent variable is the:
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome measured.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for a cohort design?

options.C: It may or may not have a control group
options.D: Subjects are followed over a period of time

questions.explanation: Randomisation belongs to experimental trials, not cohort studies.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the null hypothesis is rejected, it means that:

options.A: There is a relationship (difference) between the variables
options.B: There is no relationship between the variables

questions.explanation: Rejecting H0 supports the alternative hypothesis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the null hypothesis is accepted (not rejected), it means that:

options.A: There is no relationship between the variables
options.C: There is a relationship between the variables

questions.explanation: Failing to reject H0 means no significant relationship was found.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The nominal scale:

options.D: Ranks scores with a true zero

questions.explanation: Nominal data are labels (male/female, blood group).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The ordinal scale:

options.C: Has equal intervals and a true zero

questions.explanation: Ordinal data have order but unequal intervals (e.g. MMT grades).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The interval scale:

options.B: Rank orders with equal intervals between ranks but no true zero

questions.explanation: Temperature in Celsius is an interval scale.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The ratio scale:

options.B: Has equal intervals between ranks and a true zero point

questions.explanation: Distance walked and nerve conduction velocity are ratio data.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following measurement scales is the most precise?
questions.explanation: Ratio scales have equal intervals plus a true zero.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Manual muscle testing grades are examples of which scale of measurement?
questions.explanation: MMT grades are ranked but not equally spaced.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Goniometric measurements (degrees) are examples of which scale of measurement?
questions.explanation: Joint angles have a true zero and equal intervals.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Blood type and type of breath sound are examples of which scale of measurement?
questions.explanation: They are categories without inherent order.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The level of assistance required for a transfer (e.g. minimum, moderate) is an example of which scale?
questions.explanation: Levels of assistance rank but do not have equal spacing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In ______ sampling, all individuals have an equal chance of being selected.
questions.explanation: Simple random sampling gives every member equal probability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of probability sampling?
questions.explanation: Purposive sampling is a non-probability method.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of non-probability sampling?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is a probability method.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The type of non-probability sampling used when a rare characteristic is studied and the subjects help in identifying potential participants from existing subjects is:
questions.explanation: Snowball sampling relies on referrals from the initial subjects.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the subjects are not aware of the research hypothesis, the study is:
questions.explanation: Single blinding masks only the participants.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the subjects and some team members are not aware of the research hypothesis, the study is:
questions.explanation: Double blinding masks subjects and the investigators.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the subjects, some team members and the data analysts are not aware of the research hypothesis, the study is:
questions.explanation: Triple blinding also masks the data analysts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The degree to which the results can be applied to the general population is ______ validity.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns generalisability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the knowledge of participation by the subject affects and influences the results of an experiment, it is called the:
questions.explanation: The Hawthorne effect is a change in behaviour caused by being observed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When a test shows consistency by multiple raters, it is ______ reliability.
questions.explanation: Inter-rater reliability measures agreement between different examiners.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Consistency of rating by the same individual is ______ reliability.
questions.explanation: Intra-rater reliability is repeatability by one examiner.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Test-retest reliability measures the ______ of a test.
questions.explanation: The same test is repeated after an interval to check stability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correct?

options.A: Cohort study is prospective and case-control study is retrospective
options.D: Cohort study is retrospective and case-control is prospective

questions.explanation: Cohorts are followed forward in time; case-control studies look backward.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The average of all data scores is the:
questions.explanation: The mean is the arithmetic average.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The most frequently occurring score in a data set is the:
questions.explanation: The mode is the most common value.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The midpoint of the scores in a data set is the:
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value of ordered data.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For interval or ratio data, which measure of central tendency is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The mean uses all values and is appropriate for interval or ratio data.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For ordinal data, which measure of central tendency is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The median does not require equal intervals.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For nominal data, which measure of central tendency is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Only the most frequent category is meaningful for labels.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a normal distribution curve, ______ percent of scores lie within -1 to +1 SD.
questions.explanation: About 68 percent of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a normal distribution curve, 95 percent of scores lie within about ______ SD.
questions.explanation: 95 percent lies within two standard deviations (1.96).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a normal distribution curve, 99 percent of scores lie within about ______ SD.
questions.explanation: 99.7 percent lies within three standard deviations.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a normal distribution curve, about ______ percent of scores lie between the mean and 1 SD.
questions.explanation: Half of the 68 percent within +/-1 SD is on each side of the mean.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which measure divides data into four equal parts to determine the relative position of a score?
questions.explanation: Quartiles divide ordered data into four parts of 25 percent.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which measure divides data into 100 equal parts to determine the relative position of a score?
questions.explanation: Percentiles divide the distribution into 100 parts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for a negatively skewed distribution?

options.B: The median is to the right of the mean
options.C: The mean is to the left of the mode
options.D: The tail points to the left

questions.explanation: In negative skew the longer tail is on the left and mean < median < mode.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for a positively skewed distribution?

options.B: The tail points to the right
options.C: The median lies to the right of the mode
options.D: The mean is to the right of the mode

questions.explanation: In positive skew the longer tail is on the right.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The formula for variance is:

options.A: S squared = sum of (M - X) divided by N
options.B: S = N divided by sum of (X - M) squared
options.C: S = sum of (M - X) divided by N
options.D: S squared = sum of (X - M) squared divided by N

questions.explanation: Variance is the mean of squared deviations from the mean.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The alpha level, also known as the level of significance, is usually:
questions.explanation: Most health research sets alpha at 0.05 (sometimes 0.01).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the p-value is less than the alpha value, the null hypothesis is:
questions.explanation: A significant result rejects the null hypothesis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the p-value is more than the alpha value, the null hypothesis is:
questions.explanation: A non-significant result fails to reject the null hypothesis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A type 1 error means:

options.A: The null hypothesis is rejected despite being true
options.B: The null hypothesis is accepted despite being false
options.C: The null hypothesis is partly accepted

questions.explanation: A type 1 (alpha) error is a false positive.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A type 2 error means:

options.A: The null hypothesis is partly rejected
options.B: The null hypothesis is rejected despite being true
options.C: The null hypothesis is accepted despite being false

questions.explanation: A type 2 (beta) error is a false negative.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A type 1 (alpha) error is:
questions.explanation: Concluding a difference exists when it does not.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A type 2 (beta) error is:
questions.explanation: Missing a real difference.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding the t-test?

options.A: A two-tailed t-test evaluates both ends of the distribution
options.B: The t-test is a non-parametric test
options.C: It can be used for paired as well as independent samples
options.D: A one-tailed t-test evaluates only one end of the distribution

questions.explanation: The t-test is a parametric test.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a parametric test?
questions.explanation: Chi-square is a non-parametric test for categorical data.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correlation statistic?
questions.explanation: Chi-square tests association between categorical variables, but is not a correlation coefficient.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the variables fall in a correlation range of 0.76 to 1, the strength of the relationship is:
questions.explanation: 0.76-1.0 is a high correlation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the variables fall in a correlation range of 0.51 to 0.75, the strength of the relationship is:
questions.explanation: 0.51-0.75 is moderate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the variables fall in a correlation range of 0.26 to 0.50, the strength of the relationship is:
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the variables fall in a correlation range of 0 to 0.25, the strength of the relationship is:
questions.explanation: 0-0.25 is little or no relationship.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A positive correlation shows a ______ relationship between the variables and a negative correlation shows a ______ relationship.
questions.explanation: Positive correlation: both rise together; negative: one rises as the other falls.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A positive diagnostic test can rule IN a diagnosis, provided the test has:
questions.explanation: SpPIn: a highly specific test, when positive, rules the condition in.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A negative diagnostic test can rule OUT a diagnosis, provided the test has:
questions.explanation: SnNOut: a highly sensitive test, when negative, rules the condition out.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a normal distribution curve, the mean, median and mode lie:

options.A: On the left side of the curve
options.B: On the right side of the curve

questions.explanation: A symmetrical bell curve has all three measures at the centre.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
